transcript:
Meeting Header
Date: 2026-06-09 14:00 ET
Duration: 38 minutes
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Tomás Ruiz (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood CSM); Grace Wu (Horizon Procurement), Ethan Park (Horizon Legal), Maya Singh (Horizon CTO), Omar Khalid (Horizon DevOps)

00:00 Lena Ortiz: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. quick intro from our side, i'm lena, i'm the AE on the account, tomás is our solutions engineer, priya on CSM.
00:10 Grace Wu: Hi all, grace here. we've got ethan from legal and maya and omar on the technical side. main agenda is MSA/DPA, SLA expectations and getting pricing approved for a pilot.
00:20 Lena Ortiz: Perfect. We'll go through the MSA and DPA redline highlights, SLA appendix, and then pricing/committed options. Feel free to interrupt.
00:32 Tomás Ruiz: quick heads up on the technical side — for the pilot we propose a small dedicated pool for consistent latency, but we can discuss hosted fallbacks.
00:45 Ethan Park: from legal, i have a few redlines around liability caps and data retention. also need clarity on subpoena procedures and access controls under the DPA.
00:58 Maya Singh: and from infra, we need to confirm VPC peering and KMS integration, plus whether logs leave our region. we're EU + NA presence so data residency matters.
01:10 Lena Ortiz: understood. on KMS, we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations; we can document key rotation and that logs are only stored per region when you select residency. i'll put the exact appendix link in follow-up.
01:25 Grace Wu: can you point to SOC2 and pen test attestation? procurement needs those before approval.
01:30 Priya Nair: yes we have a SOC 2 Type II report and yearly pen test summary; we usually share an attestation and a short security package. i'll add that to the push.
01:40 Ethan Park: okay, thanks. on the MSA i wanted to walk through indemnity and export controls — also the term sheet had a clause about data for product improvement, need opt-out language in the DPA.
01:55 Lena Ortiz: sure — our standard DPA has an option to opt out of model improvement data usage; we can make that explicit. some verbiage may be a little legal-y, we'll send a redline.
02:10 Omar Khalid: technical question — for the dedicated pool, what are typical p95 latencies for a 8k context model? we need to ensure sub-300ms p95 for our UI.
02:25 Tomás Ruiz: (slight hesitation) it depends on GPU type and quantization. on Ampere-ish instances with our optimized runtime we typically see ~120-220ms p95 for a 2k step; for 8k it increases — more like 250-450ms depending on batch sizes. We'll capture specific numbers in the benchmark.
02:45 Maya Singh: that's a bit high; our UX team insists on <300ms p95 for streaming. can you guarantee that for the pilot?
02:53 Tomás Ruiz: we can target it — with dedicated A100/RTX8000 equivalents and tuned batching and prefix cache, hitting <300ms p95 for the planned prompts is realistic. we'll confirm in the benchmark run.
03:10 Grace Wu: on pricing — procurement needs committed capacity options and hosted per-token comparison. our finance prefers a predictable monthly commit.
03:20 Lena Ortiz: we have three pricing tiers: hosted pay-as-you-go, committed dedicated (monthly reserved GPUs with threshold pricing), and hybrid (dedicated baseline + burst to hosted). I'll send a spreadsheet with examples.
03:35 Ethan Park: curious about termination — if we ramp down after a quarter, what's the breakage on committed reserved?
03:42 Lena Ortiz: depends on the contract term and commit size; typical terms are 12 months with a 30% early termination fee on unused committed credits, but we can negotiate for enterprise. we'll put options in the redline.
03:55 Grace Wu: procurement also needs SLAs — availability numbers and credits; we want 99.9% for production endpoints and clear remediation path.
04:05 Priya Nair: our SLA appendix offers 99.9% standard; we also have enterprise SLAs with tighter latency SLOs and escalation paths. Credits are tiered and we provide runbook and postmortem obligations.
04:20 Ethan Park: can you share the actual SLA appendix with percentile p50/p95/p99 breakdowns and the error budget calculations?
04:28 Tomás Ruiz: yes, we'll share p50/p95/p99 latency percentiles, throughput guarantees for dedicated pools, and error budget language. we'll include how fallbacks to hosted affect SLA.
04:40 Omar Khalid: about logs and auditing — do you provide immutable audit logs and do they contain full transcripts? We can't keep full transcripts beyond thirty days for compliance.
04:50 Priya Nair: you can configure retention. default logs are 90 days but DPA can specify 30-day retention for transcripts; we can redact or not store full conversations if needed.
05:05 Ethan Park: that's important. need the DPA clause to explicitly state retention periods, deletion evidence, and right-to-audit.
05:12 Lena Ortiz: absolutely. we'll propose explicit DPA language for deletion proof and audit access.
05:22 Grace Wu: any limitations on data residency? we need EU-only processing for EU traffic.
05:30 Tomás Ruiz: we support region pinning for data processing; for private deployments we can host entirely in your VPC. For hosted we have region controls and can guarantee EU-only for selected flows. We'll put that in the DPA.
05:45 Maya Singh: on SSO and tenant isolation — we need SAML 2.0, RBAC, and per-team isolation.
05:52 Priya Nair: supported — SSO SAML, role-based access, and token scopes. We also support SCIM for provisioning.
06:00 Ethan Park: legal also flagged subcontractor lists: who else has access to data?
06:08 Lena Ortiz: typical cloud providers and our infra partners; we maintain a subcontractor list in the security package. we'll include that.
06:18 Grace Wu: ok good. back to pricing, can you show an example: 100M tokens per month, split 60/40 training vs inference? we need cost modeling to show to finance.
06:30 Lena Ortiz: yes i'll include a modeled example: hosted (pay-as-you-go) vs dedicated with a 3-rig committed pool and per-token math. spreadsheet will show monthly costs, effective per-request cost, and savings thresholds.
06:45 Omar Khalid: for the technical benchmark, what workload should we provide? short prompts vs long context?
06:50 Tomás Ruiz: provide a representative set: short routing prompts, multi-turn chat with 6-8k context, and a few heavy embedding requests. we'll run latency and cost capture and share a recorded runbook.
07:05 Maya Singh: about model versions — we need version pinning for regulatory reasons; can we pin a model and not automatically upgrade?
07:12 Tomás Ruiz: yes you can pin model versions in the deployment config; automatic upgrades are opt-in.
07:20 Ethan Park: on indemnity— we want a standard carve-out for third-party data breach that is caused by vendor negligence; also need to cap liability at a multiple of fees.
07:32 Lena Ortiz: standard commercial language is in the MSA; we can surface options for negotiating cap multiples. we'll highlight the clauses for you.
07:45 Grace Wu: when will you send the redlines? procurement wants to start approval this week.
07:50 Lena Ortiz: we'll send the redline and pricing spreadsheet by Friday, 2026-06-12.
07:58 Priya Nair: also adding SOC2 attestation and pen test summary to that package.
08:05 Ethan Park: re: DPA — show exact wording for opt-out of product improvement data usage.
08:10 Lena Ortiz: noted; we'll provide an opt-out clause.
08:15 Grace Wu: any concerns about start date? our target is to start a paid pilot July 1.
08:22 Lena Ortiz: timeline is tight but feasible; if we finalize MSA/DPA by mid-June and run the benchmark week of 6/16, we can start onboarding end of June and pilot 7/1.
08:35 Maya Singh: we'll need a quick security review after the benchmark; procurement won't sign without that.
08:40 Priya Nair: we can schedule a security walk-through with your InfoSec the week after the benchmark.
08:48 Ethan Park: also confirm if you will accept our standard audit clause language or if you prefer vendor template.
08:55 Lena Ortiz: we'll take a look and propose limited edits; we usually accept reasonable audit clauses with scheduling constraints.
09:05 Grace Wu: one last operational question — what's the escalation path for incidents? we need a named SLA contact and on-call rotation.
09:12 Priya Nair: enterprise accounts get a named Technical Account Manager and 24/7 on-call for Sev1. We'll include the escalation matrix in the SLA appendix.
09:25 Omar Khalid: small nit — will logs contain PII? we need masking options.
09:30 Tomás Ruiz: you can configure masking and redaction in the ingestion pipeline; we'll show settings in the onboarding doc.
09:38 Lena Ortiz: ok to recap next steps: we'll send redline, pricing spreadsheet, SOC2 + pen test attestation by 2026-06-12; Tomás will run benchmark plan and test on 2026-06-16; ethan will share legal redlines and retention needs by 2026-06-11.
09:58 Grace Wu: yes that sounds right. procurement will review the redline and aim to approve pricing by 6/20.
10:05 Lena Ortiz: great. i'll follow up with calendar invites for the benchmark and security walk-through. thanks everyone.
10:12 Maya Singh: thanks, bye.
10:15 Meeting ended

Notes & Links mentioned:
- SLA appendix (will be shared)
- Security package: SOC2 Type II, pen test attestation, subcontractor list
